newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 10.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 10.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Tuesday morning:
** The National Stock Exchange of India Ltd said on Monday that it declared three members as defaulters on account of their failure to fulfil their obligations
** The Economic Times newspaper says more brokers are facing difficulty to honour commitments following slump in share prices
** The World Bank-led $5 billion investment in upgrading roads sponsored by the state governments has been cleared, the Business Standard reports

** State-owned Bharat Heavy Electricals has submitted bids for captive power projects for government-run firms like Indian Oil Corporation, Gas Authority of India and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation, the Financial Express says
** The Indian rupee INR= opened steady at 35.89/90 per dollar and seen weakening, dealers say
** Indian shares ended mixed in dull trade across major bourses on Monday in the absence of investor interest amid hopes the government might initiate steps to revive markets
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index fell 11.14 points to 2,815.06
** Gold prices are likely to fall further in the Indian sub-continent with wedding season demand yet to pick up, but may firm early next year, dealers say
